blocks.a_univariate: every testable predictor x every outcome; categorical: Mann-Whitney (2 groups) or Kruskal-Wallis (3+), groups under 10 people dropped; continuous: Spearman rho with bootstrap CI
blocks.b_interactions: 18 pairs x 7 outcomes: OLS outcome ~ a + b + a:b (HC3 errors), p of the a:b term; plus site x arm (F-test of the site:arm block with a within-site permutation p); 2x2 median tables split at the median for continuous variables
blocks.c_site: per-site medians; Kruskal-Wallis over sites with 10+ people (in block a); ICC(1) with permutation p and bootstrap CI for MARD, low-range MARD, missed-low rate, CV and % time below 70; mixed model with a site random intercept, with and without covariates
blocks.d_flexible: random forest, gradient boosting and ridge; 5-fold CV x 10 repeats; feature sets: demographics only, glucose pattern only (CV, % time below 70, mean glucose), both; outcomes MARD, low-range MARD, missed-low rate; grouped permutation importance on held-out folds (not in the BH family: no p-values)
blocks.e_mediation: x -> (CV, % time below 70) -> MARD, standardised, product of coefficients, bootstrap CIs; for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c, duration, arm, prior CGM use, impaired awareness, hypo fear, fingersticks per day, number of conditions, education years (descriptive, not in the BH family)
blocks.f_worst_quartile: worst 25 % of MARD vs the rest: Mann-Whitney / Fisher / chi-square for every predictor and the glucose-pattern variables
blocks.g_shanghai: univariate tests on 20 predictors x 3 outcomes (MARD, bias, within 20/20); own BH family; no interactions or flexible models (n too small); no site variable exists in the Shanghai files

preregistration.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg over all p-values in blocks a, b, c (Kruskal-Wallis by site is in a) and f together: one family. Shanghai is a second family. p_bh within each block is also stored (secondary).
preregistration.effect_size_rule: a result that passes BH but moves the median by under 1 MARD point (or rho under 0.2) is 'statistically detectable, too small to matter'
